photos.creator: Bridge2Mi
photos.source_description: The Church of San Carpoforo is a deconsecrated church located in the bohemian Brera district. Deconsecrated in 1797, it was purchased by the municipality of Milan in 1864. In 1993 it was given for free use to the Academy of Fine Arts of Brera which uses it as a venue for the courses of decoration, restoration and contemporary sacred art.

photos.caption: Isola Bella
photos.query: Isola Bella Borromean Islands palace gardens photograph
photos.creator: Archangel12
photos.source_description: Isola Bella coming from Isola dei Pescatori. Isola Bella, named for Isabella, countess Borromeo, was originally a largely barren rock; after first improvements and buildings, opened by count Carlo III between 1629 and 1652, his son Vitaliano the 6th built an attractive summer palace, bringing in vast quantities of soil in order to build up a system of ten terraces for the garden. The unfinished building displays paintings by Lombard artists and Flemish tapestries. en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isola_Bella_ (Lago_Maggiore)
